Since commit 52d8630 (line ~2632-2736), `set` was a plain `HashSet<Alarm>`, and `disableExpiredAlarms()`/`init()` iterated `for (Alarm alarm : set)` while calling `enable()` → `changeAlarm()` → `set.remove(alarm); set.add(alarm);` inside that same loop body. content.text:
## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 52d8630f0ff645485ec9dd15cbfad88f29440f9b

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation.** The fix commit `6a2dd27` rewrites `disableExpiredAlarms`/`init()`'s expired-alarm loop and every mutating operation (`changeAlarm`, `enable`, `snooze`, `dismiss`, `create`) to call a new `writeToDb(id)` helper instead of the old `changeAlarm(Alarm)` helper. Crucially, `changeAlarm(Alarm)` used to do `set.remove(alarm); set.add(alarm);`, i.e. it mutated the very `set` collection. I traced the full history of `Alarms.java` (`git log -p --reverse`) to find when this pattern — iterating `for (Alarm alarm : set)` and calling a method that mutates `set` inside that loop — first appeared.

**(2) Root cause.** It was introduced in `52d8630` ("Model: separated AlarmsManager and Alarms"), which created `Alarms.java` with:
- `disableExpiredAlarms()`: `for (Alarm alarm : set) { ... enable(alarm.getId(), false); }`
- `enable()` → `changeAlarm(alarm)` → `set.remove(alarm); set.add(alarm);`

This means the very first execution of `disableExpiredAlarms()` (called from `init()`, i.e. at boot) that finds an expired alarm modifies `set` while a for-each loop is actively iterating over it, which throws `java.util.ConcurrentModificationException` at runtime — a real bug (app crash on boot when an expired disabled/pending alarm exists).

**(3) Evidence.** Diffing every subsequent commit that touched `Alarms.java` (`afbd98c`, `a856feb`, `2ae8486`, `cc434b6`, `7f5420e`, `49d5841`) shows this loop-plus-mutation structure was carried forward unchanged (the loop just moved from a separate `disableExpiredAlarms()` method into `init()` in `49d5841`, but the `enable()`→`changeAlarm()`→`set.remove/add` chain remained intact). Only in `6a2dd27` — the supplied fix commit — is the loop body changed to `alarm.setEnabled(false); writeToDb(alarm.getId());`, which touches the alarm's fields and the DB directly instead of calling `enable()`/`changeAlarm()`, thereby avoiding any mutation of `set` during iteration. This is a direct, minimal fix for the hazard introduced in `52d8630`.

I'm confident this is the introducing commit; I did not find an earlier point where this exact loop+mutation pattern existed (before `52d8630` the loop lived in `AlarmsManager.java` with a different structure, and I did not trace further back since the file was newly created here with the bug pattern intact from creation).
